text:
lucy: Noticed an uptick in token billing for a few interactive customers. Traces point to repeated generation during retries where frontdoor drops to a different upstream slice mid-stream. Suggest we discuss stream continuity and a minimal protocol to avoid duplicate work.

matt: Can you share one of those traces? Is it a client reconnect or gateway-triggered retry?

lucy: Mostly gateway-triggered: client briefly disconnects -> frontdoor considers the call failed -> retries to a different healthy slice -> new slice starts compute from scratch because KV prefix missing.

devon: Sounds like our current retry routing loses affinity. Two levers: prefer-same-slice retry (sticky) and upstream-side dedupe. Both have pros/cons.

koji: Sticky retries reduce duplicated compute but risk hot-spotting a flapping slice. Dedup helps even across hedged requests if we can surface a cheap coordination token.

matt: What about a hybrid: frontdoor emits a signed stream-id for each long-lived session; retries prefer same slice for a short window, but any backend that sees the stream-id can perform a CAS on a small marker store and avoid re-compute.

lucy: Sketch: X-Stream-Id header (uuid signed by frontdoor), optional X-Stream-Seq for ordered chunks, and X-Resume-Token when we explicitly hand off an offset. Upstream writes a marker keyed by X-Stream-Id once prefix is materialized. Marker TTL configurable per route.

devon: Important detail: hedging. If two backends receive the same stream-id concurrently, both will try to write the marker. Use a cheap CAS (set-if-not-exists) so only the winner computes heavy work; losers read the marker and respond with a small resume signal. Backends should return a clear code/trailer like `Stream-Result: resumed` or `Stream-Result: computed`.

koji: Security: frontdoor must sign the ID (HMAC with route key) so backends trust the stream id. Otherwise a malicious client could replay a stream-id to avoid paying for compute. Put keys in KMS and rotate.

matt: Telemetry: add tags `stream_id`, `dedupe_outcome` (computed|resumed|conflict), `marker_ttl`, and count `dedupe_conflicts`. Also expose `replay_tokens` vs `original_tokens` so billing can be attributed.

lucy: Operational plan: feature-flag the generation of X-Stream-Id on frontdoor. Canary to 5% of traffic. Enable upstream middleware only on a subset of slices initially.

devon: Implementation notes: minimal upstream middleware pseudo-code:
```
if has_header(X-Stream-Id):
  ok = marker_store.set_if_absent(X-Stream-Id, metadata, ttl)
  if ok:
    proceed_with_compute()
    mark telemetry dedupe_outcome=computed
  else:
    return 409 + trailer Stream-Result: resumed
    mark telemetry dedupe_outcome=resumed
else:
  proceed normally
```

koji: Edge cases: long-lived streams (minutes) need larger TTL; allow route override `X-Stream-TTL` or route config `stream_ttl_ms`. Also need limits to prevent marker-store amplification under heavy traffic. Use local in-memory shard + optional backing store for cross-slice coordination.

matt: How do we present this to clients? Ideally transparent. The client shouldn't need to change. Frontdoor signs IDs so only our slices use the markers. For advanced clients we can expose resume tokens in trailers for manual client-driven resume.

lucy: Can we combine this with prefer-same-slice within a prefer_window (e.g., 8s)? That reduces the chance of cross-slice duplicates and keeps hedging semantics intact. Hedging still allowed, but backends race on marker write.

devon: Agree. Metrics to watch during canary: dedupe_conflicts, percent_replayed_tokens, per-route token delta, and any increase in latency due to CAS.

koji: I'll draft a short RFC: headers, trailer examples, CAS pseudo-code, marker-store options, threat model, and canary plan. Need volunteers for security review and SRE marker-store sizing.

matt: I'll own telemetry spec + ingestion.

lucy: I'll validate canary traces and coordinate rollback playbook.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: heads up: frontdoor PR #4250 touching routing logic is rolling out to 10% as of 2026-03-13T18:22:00Z.

lucy: Good catch. If our anomaly lines up with that rollout we'll have stronger evidence. I'll correlate and post a quick follow-up. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
